intro.title: Build typed denormalization selector
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed denormalization selector function in TypeScript. This function will take a normalized data structure and transform it into a nested, easier-to-use object. You will learn how to use TypeScript's type system to ensure your selector is type-safe, catching errors at compile time. The core concepts involve working with interfaces, generics, and custom type definitions. By the end, you'll have a reusable utility that can handle structured data with full type checking.
intro.usecase: Typed denormalization selectors are essential in data-intensive applications like e-commerce dashboards, where you need to combine product data from multiple normalized API sources into a single, type-safe view. For example, when building an admin panel that displays orders with customer details and product information, selectors efficiently merge these separate data entities while maintaining TypeScript type safety. This pattern prevents runtime errors in complex filtering interfaces, such as when users search through financial transaction records that combine account, user, and payment method data. Developers use typed selectors to create reliable data transformations for real-time analytics dashboards, ensuring UI components receive properly structured, validated data.
